title: Extraction and Analysis of Low-Molecular Lipophilic Extractives in Scots Pine Sapwood
author: Olena Myronycheva
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.phqdj5w
materials: The extraction was done using acetone (VWR Chemicals: 20165.323, 75 ml) in a mini-Soxhlet extractor according to the SCAN-CM 49:03 standard method [29]. The total lipophilic extractives content was given in mg g-1 of dry mass after evaporation of the acetone and drying of the extracted solution.

steps.title: Prepare wood specimens
steps.instruction: Select all air‑dried boards and 10 randomly chosen kiln‑dried boards, cut each board to 250 mm length and 100 mm width, then split each board into four specimens.

steps.title: Plane specimens to defined depths
steps.instruction: Take three of the four specimens from each board and plane the sapwood side three times to depths of 0.25 mm, 0.75 mm and 1.75 mm measured from the original un‑planed surface.

steps.title: Mill shavings and allocate fractions
steps.instruction: Collect the shavings from each planing (3.5 g total per planing), mill them in a Fritch planetary mill, then weigh out 0.5 g for moisture‑content determination, 1.0 g for lipophilic‑compound extraction, and retain the remaining shavings for storage.

steps.title: Store remaining shavings
steps.instruction: Place the leftover shavings in a sealed container and store at –20 °C until further use.

steps.title: Extract lipophilic compounds
steps.instruction: Extract the 1.0 g of milled shavings with acetone (extraction procedure as described elsewhere) to obtain the acetone extract for subsequent analysis.

steps.title: Trimethylsilylate extracts
steps.instruction: To the acetone extract add 100 µL of BSTFA and 50 µL of TMSCl, include 1‑methylnaphthalene dissolved in pyridine as internal standard, then incubate the mixture in an oven at 70 °C for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Run GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Inject the silylated extract onto a SUPELCO SLB‑5 MS capillary column (30 m × 0.25 mm, df 0.25 µm). Use a temperature program starting at 50 °C and ramping to 270 °C, completing the run in 25 minutes. Set injector temperature to 270 °C and detector temperature to 290 °C.

steps.title: Identify and quantify acids
steps.instruction: Identify resin acids and fatty acids by matching mass spectra to the NIST Mass Spectral Library and quantify them by comparing each peak area to that of the internal standard.

steps.title: Determine total phenolics
steps.instruction: Perform the Folin‑Ciocalteu (FC) assay as described by Julkunen‑Tiitto: mix sample with reagents, incubate, then measure absorbance at 735 nm after 40 minutes against a reagent‑blank. Use tannic acid (VWR Chemicals; 83510.260) as the standard and express results as mg tannic‑acid‑equivalents (TAE) per gram dry wood.
